state.task: Assess a CanLang design change, without implementing it yet. The user wants translatable text inline wherever feasible because replacing useful # descriptions with abstract #= keys reduced readability. Adoption, token efficiency, minimal lines, one canonical mechanism and truthful business semantics are priorities. # is description metadata; ## is an ignored comment. The existing catalog requirement was an assistant decision, not a user constraint. Do not favor a proposal simply because it is new or concise.
state.audit: AST-scoped analysis of 44 sources found 724 named message rows: 699 have one actual use and 25 have two. All 373 description messages are static, have exactly one use and no other reference. Inline descriptions could remove 48 description-only import lines, totaling 1720 Unicode characters including newlines. There are 1521 generated-label rows covering 1892 targets; 256 grouped rows avoid repeating translations for 371 extra targets. Eighteen label bindings use named messages. Two exported words are shared across owners. One typed ICU plural message is reused. A matched CanDo excerpt shrinks from 42 to 32 physical lines and from 2344 to 2081 Unicode characters in one inline sketch; no model-token savings were measured. Counts establish source shape, not semantic or executable correctness.
state.research: FormatJS IntlMessageFormat accepts a message string or parsed AST directly; authored catalog keys are not necessary to format ICU messages (https://formatjs.github.io/docs/intl-messageformat/). ICU recommends whole translated messages with explicit placeholders to permit grammatical reordering (https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/messages/). Fluent documents real shared terms and grammatical-context limitations (https://projectfluent.org/fluent/guide/terms.html). These support feasibility and reuse, not a particular CanLang notation.
state.existing: Current messages tables declare en,nl columns once per owner, define typed named messages and generated-label target bindings. #= accepts only a static zero-argument message path. Ordinary # prose and string expressions stay literal. Commas already separate expression lists; | is a named-type union token, not an expression operator. Fields, parameters, enum cases and generated CRUD controls do not yet accept inline caption attributes. A composed app can have no Given body; its description currently imports another owner's message. There is a syntax parser but no semantic message checker, ICU engine, renderer, compiler or BDD executor.
state.common_contract: For the inline alternatives, choose one message-value representation for descriptions, captions, UI text and human outbound text. Add canonical label slots at declarations or adjacent owning control metadata where no authored declaration exists. Keep existing finite runtime wording defaults and schema/type caption inheritance implicit. Permit names/exports only for actual message reuse; preserve grouped bindings or equivalent reuse rather than copying 371 labels. Typed plural/placeholder arguments need explicit binding and validation; retained reusable named ICU messages already provide that boundary. Ordinary business data, routes, identifiers and fixture strings must not become translatable merely because they are strings. Compiler-derived owner/slot assets can serve browser and MCP without authored keys; machine operation and schema identities stay fixed. Inline placement alone does not prove locale coverage, ICU validity, permissions or working runtime behavior.
state.tradeoffs: A source-text suffix keeps original readable text at its use and tags translations explicitly, but repeats locale tags and requires marker escaping and a source-language rule independent of deployment default. It could use English as the pinned source baseline with an explicit owner override for other source languages; that policy is proposed, not settled. Fully keyed bundles repeat tags and quote descriptions but identify all variant languages locally. Positional bundles reduce repeated tags, but changing column order/count affects every value and requires a logical-owner locale header covering composed apps, never accidental file/deployment scope. Existing named tables centralize locale reviews, support explicit asset identities and reuse, but single-use prose requires extra keys/references/imports. Each inline spelling below is unimplemented; exact punctuation and caption-slot grammar remain open.

sketches.suffix:
# Manage team tasks. @{nl="Beheer teamtaken."}
page /tasks title="Tasks"@{nl="Taken"}
sketches.positional:
locales "en","nl"
# "Manage team tasks."|"Beheer teamtaken."
page /tasks title=("Tasks"|"Taken")
sketches.named:
#= app_description
page /tasks title=tasks_title
messages "en","nl"
 app_description = "Manage team tasks.","Beheer teamtaken."
 tasks_title = "Tasks","Taken"

feasible.instructions: Is placing static descriptions and single-use messages directly at their source sites technically feasible while preserving the supplied typing, sharing and machine-identity boundaries, provided the missing syntax and semantic/runtime work are actually implemented? Judge feasibility, not present parser support or proof of complete apps.

placement.instructions: Which representation best fits the user's inline readability and repetition goals together with independent source owners, language association and actual reuse? Weigh all supplied costs and benefits; select unresolved if the evidence cannot support a preference. This selects a design direction, not approval of unfinished exact syntax.

criteria.suffix: Keep source text/prose at use sites and attach explicitly keyed translations; retain names for genuine reuse. Accept repeated tags, source-language policy and reserved-marker/escaping work for local readability and independent locale additions.
criteria.keyed: Use inline bundles naming every language including source; retain genuine reusable assets. Accept repeated tags and quoted description text for explicit self-contained language identity without positional or implicit-source dependence.
criteria.positional: Declare locale columns per logical owner and use positional variants inline, with names for real reuse. Accept coordinated column edits and composed-app header design to minimize locale-tag repetition.
criteria.named: Continue requiring named table entries and references for all translatables. Accept single-use indirection and metadata imports for grouped locale review, explicit authored asset names and existing reuse behavior.
criteria.unresolved: Leave the representation undecided because missing source-language, label-slot or ownership contracts prevent a justified preference among these alternatives.
